stem: The vertices of a triangle are $A({=x1}, {=y1})$, $B({=x2}, {=y1})$ and $C({=x2}, {=y3})$. Find the perimeter of triangle $ABC$ in unit length.
solution: A and B have the same y-coordinate, so use the difference of the x-coordinates: $AB=|{=x2}-({=x1})|={=dx}$.
B and C have the same x-coordinate, so use the difference of the y-coordinates: $BC=|{=y3}-({=y1})|={=dy}$.
The angle at B is a right angle, so $(AC)^2=({=dx})^2+({=dy})^2={=dx*dx}+{=dy*dy}={=h*h}$ and AC = {=h}.
notes: Multi-step: two axis-parallel distances, then the distance rule, then sum. Whole-number sides via Pythagorean triples.
